reply: Your first step is to run a feasibility study on the new blend using the existing NIR probe and a Raman probe (e.g., 785 nm) in‑line, collecting spectra together with an independent reference (e.g., HPLC) to see if the NIR calibration transfers and whether Raman adds useful orthogonal information.

steps: Prepare a set of blend samples covering the expected API concentration range (e.g., 0‑[to be agreed with the customer] of target API).
Acquire reference API concentrations for each sample using the agreed reference method.
Record NIR diffuse‑reflection spectra with the existing probe under identical process conditions.
Record Raman spectra simultaneously (or sequentially) with a 785 nm probe installed at the same location.
Build an NIR‑only calibration model and evaluate prediction error on held‑out samples.
Build a Raman‑only model and evaluate similarly.
Optionally build a fused NIR+Raman model to assess any gain.
Compare model performance and decide whether the original NIR calibration can be reused or needs updating, and whether Raman adds measurable benefit.
feasibility.decisionBasis: Model validation on independent held‑out samples; performance compared to reference concentrations; acceptance criteria to be defined with the customer before testing.
